NO are soft against the run (132 yds/game allowed), and MIN feed Aaron Jones a heavy 56% carry share — a rushing-yards spot.

The NO welcome the MIN as underdogs of 1.5, with the total set at 44.5 — a market that implies a MIN 23–22 scoreline. Running the game forward from that baseline, we expect a contest that spends roughly 26% of its snaps with MIN in front, 39% within one score, and 34% with MIN chasing. That distribution is the engine of everything below: game state is what turns a team's tendencies into a specific player's workload, so before we get to individuals it's worth being explicit about how this game is likely to be played.

This is a coin-flip script. With only 1.5 points separating them, neither team projects to spend much time in a blowout state — most of the game lives in the 'close' bucket, where play-calling stays balanced and usage tracks each player's established role rather than being distorted by score. In tight games the stars on both sides see their normal, dependable workloads, and there is less garbage-time leakage to backups.

The Key Matchups

Tough sledding for Travis Etienne — MIN are stingy against the run (109 yds/game, well below the ~120 norm); lean under on his rushing line.

Sneaky value on Devaughn Vele (WR2) — MIN leak 53 yds/game to the WR2 role, above the ~36 norm.

Justin Jefferson faces a tough cover — NO hold WR1s to just 51 yds/game (vs ~58); a rec-yards under lean.

Touchdown Board

Justin Jefferson carries TD equity — NO surrender 0.47 WR1 receiving scores a game.

In the red zone MIN throw it (61% pass inside the 20) — Justin Jefferson's TD equity over a goal-line back.

Game Script, Pace & Environment

A middling 44 total — no strong lean either way; the value is in the individual matchups above, not the game environment.

Indoors — a dome removes weather variance and historically nudges passing efficiency up; a small tailwind for the passing games.

MIN — a balanced offense

MIN are a balanced offense — their run/pass split by game state tracks the league closely (42% pass when leading vs 44% average), so their players' usage is driven more by role than by any strong situational lean.

Aaron Jones (13 carries, 63 yards) projects to his baseline workload — no strong script push either way in a close game.

Justin Jefferson projects for 8 targets and 72 yards, in line with his established role in a script that neither inflates nor suppresses the pass.

Underneath, T.J. Hockenson (TE, 4 targets, 32 yards) is the dependable secondary read — and note the red zone stays TE-friendly regardless of score, so his touchdown equity holds up even if the game script shifts.

NO — a run-heavy offense

NO are one of the league's more run-committed offenses: on early downs while leading, they pass just 37% of the time, against a league average of 44% — a genuine clock-bleeding identity, not noise (it holds after shrinking their sample toward the league).

Travis Etienne (14 carries, 61 yards) projects to his baseline workload — no strong script push either way in a close game.

Chris Olave projects for 10 targets and 81 yards, in line with his established role in a script that neither inflates nor suppresses the pass.

Underneath, Juwan Johnson (TE, 5 targets, 40 yards) is the dependable secondary read — and note the red zone stays TE-friendly regardless of score, so his touchdown equity holds up even if the game script shifts.

What to watch

The single biggest swing factor is availability — use the injury tool in the sidebar to mark anyone out; a starter's absence doesn't just remove his line, it redistributes his targets and carries to specific teammates, and the report and projections rebuild around it. Beyond that: if this game breaks toward the projected 2-point margin, the garbage-time backups (the ◆-flagged rows below) are where soft lines and real edge tend to appear — those depth players get fed in blowouts, and the market is slowest to price them.

This preview and the projections below regenerate through the week as injuries, weather and line moves update the inputs.
